correctness.rationale: Chiclana's verified numerical-index identity reduces the real plane result to the stated hyperbolic maximum. For 0<α<1 the stationary product tanh(αz)tanh z grows strictly from zero to one, making its root unique, interior and analytic. Strict increase follows by testing the smaller parameter's optimizer; strict convexity follows by testing the intermediate optimizer in the two extreme objectives. At α→0, z_α=z_*+O(α²) by the stationary equation, so moving the stationary leading maximizer affects the leading term only at O(α⁵); expanding sinh gives the claimed cubic coefficient. Independent high-precision calculation gives c_*=0.66274341934918158097… and d_*=0.15897324042918032584…. The strict linear bounds follow from the two hyperbolic comparisons (or from the endpoint slopes and strict convexity), and the two limits make them sharp. At δ=1−α, u=e^(−2z_α) obeys δ=2(u^α+u)/[(1+u^α)(1+u)]. This bounds z_α by O(log(1/δ)), implies u^α/u→1 and gives u~δ/4. The objective e^(−δz_α)(1−u^α)/(1+u) gives the deficit, and the ratio cosh(αz_α)/cosh z_α=1+O(δ log(1/δ)) gives the separately justified envelope derivative asymptotic. With t_p=u^(1/p), δ=2(p−1)/p or 2/p gives both migrations; the small power of u near p=1 differs from u by a factor tending to one. Frozen check.py was inspected, not executed.
